focusSummary: Core polite greetings, high-leverage survival responses (すみません, お願いします, 大丈夫です), konbini checkout decoding, and essential entrance/exit signage.

lessonSteps.heading: Time-of-Day Greetings & Polite Gratitude
lessonSteps.explanation: Adding ございます makes morning and thank-you greetings polite enough for hotel front desks, shop clerks, and strangers alike. こんにちは works from late morning until dusk.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You walk past your hotel front desk at 8:30 AM and receive a city map from the receptionist.
lessonSteps.nativeText: おはようございます。ありがとうございます。
lessonSteps.translation: Good morning. Thank you very much.
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: おはよう (early) + ございます (polite copula) / ありがとう (rare/precious) + ございます (polite)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Drop ございます only with close friends or family; with staff or strangers, keep the full polite form.

lessonSteps.heading: The Swiss-Army Survival Pair: すみません & お願いします
lessonSteps.explanation: すみません means 'Excuse me', 'Sorry', and even 'Thank you for going out of your way'. Pair it with お願いします ('Please, I entrust this to you') whenever handing over items, cards, or requests.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You want to catch a clerk's attention at the register and ask to pay.
lessonSteps.nativeText: すみません、これをお願いします。
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: すみません、これをお<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします。
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: すみません (excuse me) + これ (this) + を (object marker) + お願いします (humbly request)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Whenever a clerk asks if you want a bag or warming and you DO want it, answer warmly: 「はい、お願いします。」

lessonSteps.heading: Polite Declining Without Saying 'No': 大丈夫です
lessonSteps.explanation: Direct いいえ ('No') can sound abrupt at a counter. Instead, Japanese speakers smile slightly and say 大丈夫です ('It's alright / I'm good') to decline plastic bags, receipts, or chopsticks.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: The konbini clerk holds up a plastic shopping bag and asks 「袋にお入れしますか？」 ('Shall I put this in a bag?'). You have your own backpack.
lessonSteps.nativeText: 大丈夫です。ありがとうございます。
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: <ruby>大丈夫<rt>だいじょうぶ</rt></ruby>です。ありがとうございます。
lessonSteps.translation: No thank you, I'm fine. Thank you.
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: 大丈夫 (safe / all right) + です (is) + ありがとうございます (thank you)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Adding a light hand wave near your chest or a small nod makes it unmistakable that you are declining politely.

lessonSteps.heading: Reading Doorway Signage: 入口, 出口 & 営業中
lessonSteps.explanation: Three visual Kanji compounds unlock almost every shop door in Japan: 入 ('enter') + 口 ('opening/door') = 入口 (entrance); 出 ('exit/go out') + 口 = 出口 (exit); and 営業中 ('currently in business' = Open).
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You approach a busy glass storefront with two sliding doors and a wooden plaque hanging in the window.
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: <ruby>入口<rt>いりぐち</rt></ruby>・<ruby>出口<rt>でぐち</rt></ruby>・<ruby>営業中<rt>えいぎょうちゅう</rt></ruby>
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: 入口 (enter-mouth) / 出口 (exit-mouth) / 営業 (business operations) + 中 (in progress)
lessonSteps.usageTip: If the sign flips to 準備中 (じゅんびちゅう, 'in preparation'), the shop is temporarily closed between lunch and dinner service.

drills.prompt: The konbini clerk points to your bento box and asks 「お弁当温めますか？」 ('Shall I warm up your bento?'). How do you say 'Yes, please'?
drills.explanation: 「はい、お願いします」 (Hai, onegaishimasu) is the natural, polite way to accept an offer of service such as warming food or receiving a bag.

drills.prompt: Next, the clerk asks 「袋にお入れしますか？」 ('Would you like a bag?'), and you already have a tote bag. Choose the most natural polite refusal.
drills.cue: Decline smoothly ('I'm fine / No thank you')
options: すみません、お願いします。
acceptedVariants: 大丈夫です。ありがとうございます。
drills.explanation: 「大丈夫です」 (Daijōbu desu) softly declines bags, receipts, or point cards without the bluntness of a bare 「いいえ」.

drills.prompt: You have finished shopping and want to walk out through the correct one-way automatic door. Which sign marks the exit?
drills.explanation: 出 (de, go out) + 口 (guchi, doorway) forms 出口 (deguchi, Exit), whereas 入口 (iriguchi) means Entrance.

gradedStories.title: あさのコンビニ
gradedStories.setting: 8:15 AM at a bright neighborhood convenience store near your Tokyo hotel.

paragraphs.nativeText: 「営業中」のサインを見て、コンビニの入口から入ります。「おはようございます！」と店員さんが言います。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: 「<ruby>営業中<rt>えいぎょうちゅう</rt></ruby>」のサインを<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>て、コンビニの<ruby>入口<rt>いりぐち</rt></ruby>から<ruby>入<rt>はい</rt></ruby>ります。「おはようございます！」と<ruby>店員<rt>てんいん</rt></ruby>さんが<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>います。
paragraphs.translation: Seeing the 'Open for Business' sign, I walk in through the convenience store entrance. 'Good morning!' says the clerk.

paragraphs.nativeText: わたしはお弁当とコーヒーをレジに置きます。店員さんが「お弁当温めますか？」と聞きます。わたしは「はい、お願いします」と答えます。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: わたしはお<ruby>弁当<rt>べんとう</rt></ruby>とコーヒーをレジに<ruby>置<rt>お</rt></ruby>きます。<ruby>店員<rt>てんいん</rt></ruby>さんが「お<ruby>弁当<rt>べんとう</rt></ruby><ruby>温<rt>あたた</rt></ruby>めますか？」と<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>きます。わたしは「はい、お<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします」と<ruby>答<rt>こた</rt></ruby>えます。
paragraphs.translation: I place a bento box and coffee at the register. The clerk asks, 'Shall I warm up your bento?' I answer, 'Yes, please.'

paragraphs.nativeText: 「袋にお入れしますか？」と聞かれて、「大丈夫です。タッチ決済でお願いします」と言います。「ありがとうございます」と言って、出口から出ます。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: 「<ruby>袋<rt>ふくろ</rt></ruby>にお<ruby>入<rt>い</rt></ruby>れしますか？」と<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>かれて、「<ruby>大丈夫<rt>だいじょうぶ</rt></ruby>です。タッチ<ruby>決済<rt>けっさい</rt></ruby>でお<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします」と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>います。「ありがとうございます」と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>って、<ruby>出口<rt>でぐち</rt></ruby>から<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>ます。
paragraphs.translation: Asked 'Shall I put this in a bag?', I say 'I'm fine. Contactless payment, please.' Saying 'Thank you very much,' I head out through the exit.

Took a bag and paid with a point card
Declined the bag and paid by contactless tap payment

referenceSheets.title: Konbini Clerk Decoder
referenceSheets.subtitle: Decode rapid-fire register questions and answer smoothly in two words

rows.rubyHtml: <ruby>袋<rt>ふくろ</rt></ruby>にお<ruby>入<rt>い</rt></ruby>れしますか？
rows.readingOrSubtle: Fukuro ni o-ire shimasu ka? (also: レジ袋はご利用ですか？)
rows.meaning: Would you like a shopping bag? (bags cost ¥3–¥5)
rows.exampleNative: はい、お願いします。 / 大丈夫です。
rows.exampleTranslation: Yes, please. / No thank you, I'm fine.
rows.notes: Listen for the keyword ふくろ (fukuro = bag).

rows.rubyHtml: お<ruby>弁当<rt>べんとう</rt></ruby><ruby>温<rt>あたた</rt></ruby>めますか？
rows.meaning: Shall I warm up your bento / meal?
rows.notes: Listen for あたため (atatame = warming). Clerks microwave it behind the counter for you.

rows.term: ポイントカードはお持ちですか？
rows.rubyHtml: ポイントカードはお<ruby>持<rt>も</rt></ruby>ちですか？
rows.readingOrSubtle: Pointo kādo wa o-mochi desu ka?
rows.meaning: Do you have a loyalty point card?
rows.exampleNative: 大丈夫です。 / 持っていないです。
rows.exampleTranslation: I'm fine (don't have one). / I don't have one.
rows.notes: Listen for ポイントカード; almost all travelers simply smile and say 「大丈夫です」.

rows.term: お箸はお付けしますか？
rows.rubyHtml: お<ruby>箸<rt>はし</rt></ruby>はお<ruby>付<rt>つ</rt></ruby>けしますか？
rows.exampleNative: はい、一膳お願いします。 / 大丈夫です。
rows.exampleTranslation: Yes, one pair please. / No thank you.
rows.notes: Clerks may also offer スプーン (supūn, spoon) or おしぼり (oshibori, wet wipe).

rows.term: タッチ決済でお願いします。
rows.rubyHtml: タッチ<ruby>決済<rt>けっさい</rt></ruby>でお<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします。
rows.meaning: Contactless tap payment (Visa/Mastercard/Apple Pay credit tap), please.
rows.exampleNative: クレジットカードのタッチ決済でお願いします。
rows.exampleTranslation: By credit card tap payment, please.
rows.notes: Saying 「クレジットカードのタッチで」 tells the terminal to expect contactless NFC credit rather than an IC transit card.

rows.term: 画面のタッチをお願いします。
rows.rubyHtml: <ruby>画面<rt>がめん</rt></ruby>のタッチをお<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします。
rows.meaning: Please tap the confirmation button on the screen (age verification for alcohol).
rows.notes: When buying beer or chūhai, tap 「はい」 (20 years or older) on the customer-facing touchscreen.

referenceSheets.title: Core Particles
referenceSheets.subtitle: Eight tiny postpositions that snap Japanese words into crystal-clear roles

rows.readingOrSubtle: Written は, pronounced 'wa' as a particle
rows.meaning: Topic marker — sets the stage ('As for X...')
rows.exampleNative: わたしはコーヒーをお願いします。
rows.notes: Contrasts or introduces what the sentence is about.

rows.meaning: Subject / spotlight marker — pinpoints new info, existence, or ability
rows.exampleTranslation: There is an ATM right here.
rows.notes: Always pairs with あります / います ('there is') and わかります ('understand').

rows.meaning: Direct object marker — marks the thing acted upon
rows.notes: In casual spoken Japanese or fast counter phrases, を is sometimes dropped, but keeping it is crystal clear.

rows.meaning: Pinpoint target — destination, exact time, or static location
rows.exampleNative: 袋に入れます。七時に着きます。
rows.exampleTranslation: Put into a bag. Arrive at 7 o'clock.
rows.notes: Think of に as a pin dropped on a map or clock.

rows.meaning: Arena of action OR tool/means ('at/in' for actions; 'by/with' for payment or transport)
rows.exampleNative: コンビニで買います。カードで払います。
rows.exampleTranslation: Buy at the konbini. Pay by card.
rows.notes: Use で (not に) when an active event happens inside a place, or when naming your payment method.

rows.readingOrSubtle: Written へ, pronounced 'e' as a particle
rows.notes: Highlights the direction of travel rather than arrival.

rows.meaning: Complete 'and' between nouns; 'with' a companion; quotation marker
rows.exampleNative: お水とお茶をください。
rows.notes: Connects nouns — never two full verbs/sentences.

rows.meaning: Noun linker / possession ('X's Y' or 'Y of X')
rows.notes: The modifier always comes BEFORE の, and the main noun comes AFTER の.
